description: Decision rules for the Equal Care Navigator. Part 1 links a measured gap to a measure from the national implementation roadmap 2026-2031. Part 2 sorts every gap by how relevant it is for a decision. The rules decide; the AI model only explains the result. Every proposal is something to evaluate, not a proven remedy: the data shows where a gap is, not what causes it.

group_gap.description: A gap measured directly between two population groups for all of Finland (evidence type A), newest full year only.

fields.robust: yes if the 95 % confidence interval of the gap lies above zero, otherwise no

pathway_data.description: Whether open data exists for the stages referral, diagnosis and start of treatment.

fields.pathway_data_missing: yes if at least one of these stages has no open data, otherwise no

region_below_target.description: A wellbeing services county that is clearly below the 80 % participation target in at least one screening programme.

fields.language_level: disadvantaged if the county is in the third with the most other-language speakers, otherwise middle or advantaged
fields.education_level: disadvantaged if the county is in the third with the lowest education level, otherwise middle or advantaged

region_access.description: Every wellbeing services county, whatever its screening participation.

fields.primary_care_access_level: disadvantaged if the county is in the third with the longest waits for a non-urgent doctor appointment

gap_relevance.description: Any gap the project knows of: a difference between population groups, a region below the screening target, a pattern between areas, a waiting time above the national guidance, a barrier documented in strategy texts, or missing data.

fields.evidence: group_measured_robust (difference between groups, 95 % interval above zero); target_shortfall (region clearly below the 80 % target); regional_pattern_robust (pattern between areas that survives the correction for many comparisons); group_measured_uncertain; regional_pattern_not_robust; single_source_measured (one hospital or one study); documented_only (strategy texts); no_open_data
fields.size: large, medium, small or unknown, from the bands for size_points
fields.reach: large, medium, small or unknown, from the bands for reach_people

levels.high: Measured directly, clearly larger than chance, large, and many people affected. Act on it first.
levels.medium: Measured and clearly larger than chance, but smaller, affecting fewer people, or only visible as a pattern between areas.
levels.low: Measured and clearly larger than chance, but small.
levels.uncertain: A difference is visible but could be chance, or rests on a single source. Watch it; do not act on it alone.
levels.not_measurable: No open data allows a measurement. This is not the same as unimportant: the problem may be large. The first step is to make it measurable.

bands.note: Thresholds that turn a number into large, medium or small. They are judgement calls of the project team and can be changed here.

size_points.meaning: Difference in percentage points between the two groups, or distance to the 80 % target.

reach_people.meaning: People in the disadvantaged group who are affected in one year, for example invited to screening.

challenge_pathway.note: Where each pathway stage used in the data sits in the AstraZeneca challenge: its four pathway points (detection, referral from primary to specialist care, diagnosis, treatment initiation) and its three named bottlenecks.
